questions.question: Why is it not legal to transmit a 3 kHz bandwidth USB signal with a carrier frequency of 14.348 MHz?
answers: USB is not used on 20-meter phone
The lower 1 kHz of the signal is outside the 20-meter band
The upper 1 kHz of the signal is outside the 20-meter band
questions.explanation: The 20 m band ends at 14.350 MHz (§97.301). A USB signal occupies the carrier frequency up to about 3 kHz above it, so with the carrier at 14.348 MHz the signal extends to 14.351 MHz, putting the top 1 kHz outside the band.

questions.question: When using a transceiver that displays the carrier frequency of phone signals, which of the following displayed frequencies represents the lowest frequency at which a properly adjusted LSB emission will be totally within the band?
answers: 300 Hz above the lower band edge
1 kHz above the lower band edge
3 kHz above the lower band edge
questions.explanation: LSB puts the signal energy below the displayed carrier frequency, roughly 3 kHz wide. So the carrier has to be at least 3 kHz above the lower edge of the phone segment for the whole emission to stay inside it (§97.301, §97.305).

questions.question: What is the highest legal carrier frequency on the 20-meter band for transmitting a 2.8 kHz wide USB data signal?
questions.explanation: The 20 m data segment ends at 14.150 MHz (§97.305). A USB signal sits above the carrier, so the carrier can be no higher than 14.150 − 0.0028 = 14.1472 MHz.

questions.question: May an Extra class operator answer the CQ of a station on 3.601 MHz LSB phone?
answers: Yes, the entire signal will be inside the SSB allocation for Extra class operators
Yes, the displayed frequency is within the 75-meter phone band segment
No, the sideband components will extend beyond the edge of the phone band segment
No, US stations are not permitted to use phone emissions below 3.610 MHz
questions.explanation: The 75 m phone segment starts at 3.600 MHz. An LSB signal with its carrier at 3.601 MHz extends about 3 kHz below it, to roughly 3.598 MHz, so part of it falls outside the phone segment.
questions.explanationNote: Assumes the LSB occupied bandwidth is ~3 kHz.

questions.question: Who must be in physical control of the station apparatus of an amateur station aboard any vessel or craft that is documented or registered in the United States?
answers: Only a person with an FCC Marine Radio license grant
Only a person named in an amateur station license grant
Any person holding an FCC issued amateur license or who is authorized for alien reciprocal operation
Any person named in an amateur station license grant or a person holding an unrestricted Radiotelephone Operator Permit
questions.explanation: Under §97.5(a)(2), an amateur station on a US-documented vessel or craft must be under the physical control of someone holding an FCC-issued amateur license or authorized for alien reciprocal operation. No other license or permit is needed.

questions.question: What is the required transmit frequency of a CW signal for channelized 60 meter operation?
answers: At the lowest frequency of the channel
At the center frequency of the channel
At the highest frequency of the channel
On any frequency where the signal’s sidebands are within the channel
questions.explanation: §97.303(h)(1) requires 60 m CW emissions to be centered on the channel center frequency. Since a CW signal is just the carrier, you transmit right on the center frequency.

questions.question: What is the maximum power permitted on the 2200-meter band?
questions.explanation: §97.313(k) limits 2200 m (135.7–137.8 kHz) stations to 1 W EIRP.

questions.question: If a station in a message forwarding system inadvertently forwards a message that is in violation of FCC rules, who is primarily accountable for the rules violation?
answers: The control operator of the packet bulletin board station
The control operator of the originating station
The control operators of all the stations in the system
The control operators of all the stations in the system not authenticating the source from which they accept communications
questions.explanation: §97.219(b): in a message forwarding system, the control operator of the originating station is primarily accountable for any violation. Forwarding stations that pass a violating message on inadvertently are not held accountable.

questions.question: Except in some parts of Alaska, what is the maximum power permitted on the 630-meter band?
questions.explanation: §97.313(l) limits 630 m (472–479 kHz) stations to 5 W EIRP. Stations in parts of Alaska close to Russia are limited to 1 W EIRP.

questions.question: If an amateur station is installed aboard a ship or aircraft, what condition must be met before the station is operated?
answers: Its operation must be approved by the master of the ship or the pilot in command of the aircraft
The amateur station operator must agree not to transmit when the main radio of the ship or aircraft is in use
The amateur station must have a power supply that is completely independent of the main ship or aircraft power supply
The amateur station must operate only in specific segments of the amateur service HF and VHF bands
questions.explanation: §97.11(a) requires that an amateur station aboard a ship or aircraft be operated only with the approval of the ship's master or the aircraft's pilot in command. Its installation must also be separate from the vessel's main radio equipment.

questions.question: What licensing is required when operating an amateur station aboard a US-registered vessel in international waters?
answers: Any amateur license with an FCC Marine or Aircraft endorsement
Only General class or higher amateur licenses
questions.explanation: §97.5(a)(2): on a US-registered vessel, any person holding an FCC-issued amateur license, of any class, may operate. No marine endorsement or commercial permit is required.

questions.question: Which of the following constitutes a spurious emission?
answers: An amateur station transmission made without the proper call sign identification
A signal transmitted to prevent its detection by any station other than the intended recipient
Any transmitted signal that unintentionally interferes with another licensed radio station and whose levels exceed 40 dB below the fundamental power level
An emission outside the signal’s necessary bandwidth that can be reduced or eliminated without affecting the information transmitted
questions.explanation: §97.3(a)(43) defines a spurious emission as an emission on frequencies outside the necessary bandwidth whose level can be reduced without affecting the information being transmitted. Harmonics, parasitics and intermodulation products are examples.

questions.question: Which of the following is an acceptable bandwidth for digital voice or slow-scan TV transmissions made on the HF amateur bands?
questions.explanation: Digital voice and SSTV on HF must not take up more bandwidth than a typical voice SSB signal, which is about 3 kHz (§97.307(f)(2)).

questions.question: Within what distance must an amateur station protect an FCC monitoring facility from harmful interference?
questions.explanation: §97.13: a station within 1 mile of an FCC monitoring facility must protect it from harmful interference.

questions.question: What must the control operator of a repeater operating in the 70-centimeter band do if a radiolocation system experiences interference from that repeater?
answers: Reduce the repeater antenna HAAT (Height Above Average Terrain)
File an FAA NOTAM (Notice to Air Missions) with the repeater system's ERP, call sign, and six-character grid locator
Cease operation or make changes to the repeater that mitigate the interference
questions.explanation: Amateurs are secondary in 70 cm, and government radiolocation is primary (§97.303(b)). A repeater causing interference must stop transmitting or be modified until the interference is resolved.

questions.question: What is the National Radio Quiet Zone?
answers: An area surrounding the FCC monitoring station in Laurel, Maryland
An area in New Mexico surrounding the White Sands Test Area
An area surrounding the National Radio Astronomy Observatory
An area in Florida surrounding Cape Canaveral
questions.explanation: The National Radio Quiet Zone protects the radio telescopes at Green Bank, WV (NRAO) and the Navy facility at Sugar Grove. It covers parts of West Virginia and Virginia (§97.3(a)(33), §97.203(e)).

questions.question: Which of the following additional rules apply if you are erecting an amateur station antenna structure at a site at or near a public use airport?
answers: You may have to notify the Federal Aviation Administration and register it with the FCC as required by Part 17 of the FCC rules
You may have to enter the height above ground in meters, and the latitude and longitude in degrees, minutes, and seconds on the FAA website
You must file an Environmental Impact Statement with the EPA before construction begins
You must obtain a construction permit from the airport zoning authority per Part 119 of the FAA regulations
questions.explanation: §97.15(a): antenna structures near public-use airports may need FAA notification and FCC registration (ASR) under 47 CFR Part 17, depending on height and distance from the runway.

questions.question: To what type of regulations does PRB-1 apply?
answers: Use of wireless devices in vehicles
questions.explanation: PRB-1 (codified at §97.15(b)) preempts state and local zoning that does not reasonably accommodate amateur antennas. It does not cover private restrictions such as HOA covenants.

questions.question: What limitations may the FCC place on an amateur station if its signal causes interference to domestic broadcast reception, assuming that the receivers involved are of good engineering design?
answers: The amateur station must cease operation
The amateur station must cease operation on all frequencies below 30 MHz
The amateur station must cease operation on all frequencies above 30 MHz
The amateur station must avoid transmitting during certain hours on frequencies that cause the interference
questions.explanation: §97.121(a): if a station interferes with domestic broadcast reception on well-engineered receivers, the FCC can impose quiet hours. These are periods when the station must not transmit on the offending frequencies.

questions.question: Which amateur stations may be operated under RACES rules?
answers: Only those club stations licensed to Amateur Extra class operators
Any FCC-licensed amateur station except a Technician class
Any FCC-licensed amateur station certified by the responsible civil defense organization for the area served
Only stations meeting the FCC Part 97 technical standards for operation during an emergency
questions.explanation: §97.407(a): any FCC-licensed amateur station may operate in RACES if it is certified by the responsible civil defense organization for the area served.

questions.question: What frequencies are authorized to an amateur station operating under RACES rules?
answers: All amateur service frequencies authorized to the control operator
Specific segments in the amateur service MF, HF, VHF, and UHF bands
questions.explanation: §97.407(b): a RACES station may use all amateur frequencies its control operator is authorized to use, except that RACES drills and tests may be restricted.

questions.question: What does PRB-1 require of state and local regulations affecting amateur radio antenna size and structures?
answers: No limitations may be placed on antenna size or placement
Reasonable accommodations of amateur radio must be made
Such structures must be permitted when use for emergency communications can be demonstrated
Such structures must be permitted if certified by a registered professional engineer
questions.explanation: PRB-1 (§97.15(b)) requires state and local regulations on amateur antennas to reasonably accommodate amateur communications, using the minimum practicable regulation needed for the local authority's legitimate purpose.

questions.question: What is the maximum bandwidth for a data emission on 60 meters?
questions.explanation: On the 60 m channels, data emissions may be no wider than 2.8 kHz (§97.303(h)).

questions.question: Which of the following apply to communications transmitted to amateur stations in foreign countries?
answers: Third party traffic must be limited to that intended for the exclusive use of government and non-Government Organization (NGOs) involved in emergency relief activities
All transmissions must be in English
Communications must be limited to those incidental to the purpose of the amateur service and remarks of a personal nature
questions.explanation: §97.117: communications with foreign amateur stations must be limited to those incidental to the purposes of the amateur service, plus remarks of a personal character.

questions.question: How long must an operator wait after filing a notification with the Utilities Technology Council (UTC) before operating on the 2200-meter or 630-meter band?
answers: Operators must not operate until approval is received
Operators may operate after 30 days, providing they have not been told that their station is within 1 kilometer of PLC systems using those frequencies
Operators may not operate until a test signal has been transmitted in coordination with the local power company
Operations may commence immediately, and may continue unless interference is reported by the UTC
questions.explanation: §97.303(g): after notifying the UTC, a station may operate on 630 m or 2200 m after 30 days unless UTC has said it is within 1 km of a PLC system using those frequencies.

questions.question: What is an IARP?
answers: A permit that allows US amateurs to operate in certain countries of the Americas
The internal amateur radio practices policy of the FCC
An indication of increased antenna reflected power
A forecast of intermittent aurora radio propagation
questions.explanation: The IARP (International Amateur Radio Permit) is issued under a CITEL (Inter-American) convention. It lets a US amateur operate in participating countries of the Americas without getting a separate license.

questions.question: Under what situation may a station transmit third party communications while being automatically controlled?
answers: Only when transmitting RTTY or data emissions
Only when transmitting SSB or CW
On any mode approved by the National Telecommunication and Information Administration
questions.explanation: §97.115(c): no station may transmit third-party communications while automatically controlled, except when transmitting RTTY or data emissions.

questions.question: Which of the following is required in order to operate in accordance with CEPT rules in foreign countries where permitted?
answers: You must identify in the official language of the country in which you are operating
The US embassy must approve of your operation
You must have a copy of FCC Public Notice DA 16-1048
You must append "/CEPT" to your call sign
questions.explanation: Operating under CEPT T/R 61-01 requires carrying FCC Public Notice DA 16-1048, along with proof of US citizenship and your FCC license.

questions.question: What notifications must be given before transmitting on the 630- or 2200-meter bands?
answers: A special endorsement must be requested from the FCC
An environmental impact statement must be filed with the Department of the Interior
Operators must inform the FAA of their intent to operate, giving their call sign and distance to the nearest runway
Operators must inform the Utilities Technology Council (UTC) of their call sign and coordinates of the station
questions.explanation: §97.303(g) requires you to notify the Utilities Technology Council of your call sign and station coordinates before operating on 630 m or 2200 m.

questions.question: What is the maximum permissible duration of a remotely controlled station’s transmissions if its control link malfunctions?
questions.explanation: §97.213(b): a remotely controlled station must stop transmitting within 3 minutes if its control link fails.

questions.question: What is the highest modulation index permitted at the highest modulation frequency for angle modulation below 29.0 MHz?
questions.explanation: §97.307(f)(1) limits angle modulation below 29 MHz to a maximum modulation index of 1 at the highest modulating frequency.

questions.question: What is the maximum mean power level for a spurious emission below 30 MHz with respect to the fundamental emission?
questions.explanation: §97.307(d): for transmitters installed after Jan 1, 2003, spurious emissions below 30 MHz must be at least 43 dB below the mean power of the fundamental.

questions.question: Which of the following operating arrangements allows an FCC-licensed US citizen to operate in many European countries, and amateurs from many European countries to operate in the US?
questions.explanation: Under the CEPT recommendation T/R 61-01, US citizens can operate in participating European countries, and CEPT licensees can operate in the US under §97.5 and §97.107 reciprocal provisions.

questions.question: In what portion of the 630-meter band are phone emissions permitted?
questions.explanation: §97.305(c) authorizes phone, CW, RTTY and data across the whole 630 m band (472–479 kHz).

questions.question: What is the definition of telemetry?
answers: One-way transmission of measurements at a distance from the measuring instrument
Two-way transmissions in excess of 1000 feet
One-way transmission that initiates, modifies, or terminates the functions of a device at a distance
questions.explanation: §97.3(a)(46) defines telemetry as a one-way transmission of measurements at a distance from the measuring instrument.

questions.question: Which of the following may transmit encrypted messages?
answers: Telecommand signals from a space telecommand station
Auxiliary relay links carrying repeater audio
questions.explanation: §97.211(b) lets space telecommand stations transmit special codes intended to obscure the meaning of command messages to a space station. This is a narrow exception to the general ban on encryption.

questions.question: What is a space telecommand station?
answers: An amateur station located on the surface of the Earth for communication with other Earth stations by means of Earth satellites
An amateur station that transmits communications to initiate, modify, or terminate functions of a space station
An amateur station located in a satellite or a balloon more than 50 kilometers above the surface of the Earth
An amateur station that receives telemetry from a satellite or balloon more than 50 kilometers above the surface of the Earth
questions.explanation: §97.3(a)(44): a telecommand station transmits communications that initiate, modify or terminate functions of a device at a distance. A space telecommand station does this for a space station.

questions.question: Which of the following is required in the identification transmissions from a balloon-borne telemetry station?
answers: The output power of the balloon transmitter
The station's six-character Maidenhead grid locator
questions.explanation: §97.119(a) requires every station, including a balloon-borne telemetry station, to identify by transmitting its call sign. Power and grid locator are not required.

questions.question: What must be posted at the location of a station being operated by telecommand on or within 50 kilometers of the Earth’s surface?
answers: A photocopy of the station license
A label with the name, address, and telephone number of the station licensee
A label with the name, address, and telephone number of the control operator
questions.explanation: §97.213(d) requires a station operated by telecommand on or within 50 km of Earth's surface to post a photocopy of the license and labels with the licensee's and control operator's names, addresses and phone numbers, so all three choices are correct.

questions.question: What is the maximum permitted transmitter output power when operating a model craft by telecommand?
questions.explanation: §97.215(c) limits the transmitter output power for telecommand of model craft to 1 W.

questions.question: Which of the following HF amateur bands include allocations for space stations?
answers: Satellite operation is permitted on all HF bands
questions.explanation: §97.207(c) authorizes space stations on 40 m, 20 m, 17 m, 15 m, 12 m and 10 m. Among the HF choices given, the correct set is 40, 20, 15 and 10 m.

questions.question: Which VHF amateur bands have frequencies authorized for space stations?
questions.explanation: §97.207(c)(2): the only VHF space-station allocation is 2 m (144–146 MHz).

questions.question: Which UHF amateur bands have frequencies authorized for space stations?
questions.explanation: §97.207(c)(2): the UHF space-station allocations are 435–438 MHz (70 cm) and 2400–2450 MHz (13 cm).

questions.question: Which amateur stations are eligible to be telecommand stations of space stations, subject to the privileges of the class of operator license held by the control operator of the station?
answers: Any amateur station approved by AMSAT
Any amateur station so designated by the space station licensee
Any amateur station so designated by the ITU
questions.explanation: §97.211(a): any amateur station designated by the space station licensee may be a telecommand station, within the privileges of its control operator.

questions.question: Which amateur stations are eligible to operate as Earth stations?
answers: Any amateur licensee who has successfully completed the AMSAT space communications course
Only those of General, Advanced or Amateur Extra class operators
Only those of Amateur Extra class operators
Any amateur station, subject to the privileges of the class of operator license held by the control operator
questions.explanation: §97.209(a): any amateur station may be an Earth station, within the privileges of its control operator's license class.

questions.question: Which of the following amateur stations may transmit one-way communications?
answers: A space station, beacon station, or telecommand station
A local repeater or linked repeater station
A message forwarding station or automatically controlled digital station
questions.explanation: One-way communications are specifically authorized for space stations (§97.207(e)), beacons (§97.203(g)) and, via §97.111(b), telecommand stations.
questions.explanationNote: Telecommand one-way authority attributed to §97.111(b) (text truncated in our eCFR check); space station §97.207(e) and beacon §97.203(g) verified.

questions.question: For which types of out-of-pocket expenses do the Part 97 rules state that VEs and VECs may be reimbursed?
answers: Preparing, processing, administering, and coordinating an examination for an amateur radio operator license
Teaching an amateur operator license examination preparation course
No expenses are authorized for reimbursement
Providing amateur operator license examination preparation training materials
questions.explanation: §97.527: VEs and VECs may be reimbursed for out-of-pocket expenses of preparing, processing, administering and coordinating examinations, but not for training courses or materials.

questions.question: Who is tasked by Part 97 with maintaining the pools of questions for all US amateur license examinations?
questions.explanation: §97.523: all VECs must cooperate in maintaining one question pool for each written element. The NCVEC Question Pool Committee does this work.

questions.question: What is a Volunteer Examiner Coordinator?
answers: A person who has volunteered to administer amateur operator license examinations
An organization paid by the volunteer examiner team to publicize and schedule examinations
An organization that has entered into an agreement with the FCC to coordinate, prepare, and administer amateur operator license examinations
The person who has entered into an agreement with the FCC to be the VE session manager
questions.explanation: §97.521: a VEC is an organization that has entered into an agreement with the FCC to coordinate amateur license examination efforts.

questions.question: What is required to be accredited as a Volunteer Examiner?
answers: Each General, Advanced and Amateur Extra class operator is automatically accredited as a VE when the license is granted
The amateur operator applying must pass a VE examination administered by the FCC Enforcement Bureau
The prospective VE must obtain accreditation from the FCC
A VEC must confirm that the VE applicant meets FCC requirements to serve as an examiner
questions.explanation: §97.509 and §97.525: a VE must be accredited by a VEC, which checks that the applicant meets the FCC requirements (license class, age, no revocation history, and so on).

questions.question: What must the VE team do with the application form if the examinee does not pass the exam?
answers: Maintain the application form with the VEC’s records
Return the application document to the examinee
Send the application form to the FCC and inform the FCC of the grade
questions.explanation: §97.509(j): if the examinee does not pass, the VEs return the application document to the examinee and tell them the grade.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the proper conduct and necessary supervision during an amateur operator license examination session?
questions.explanation: §97.509(c): each administering VE is responsible for the proper conduct and necessary supervision of the exam session.

questions.question: What should a VE do if a candidate fails to comply with the examiner’s instructions during an amateur operator license examination?
answers: Warn the candidate that continued failure to comply will result in termination of the examination
Allow the candidate to complete the examination, but invalidate the results
Immediately terminate everyone’s examination and close the session
questions.explanation: §97.509(c): administering VEs must immediately terminate the exam of any examinee who fails to follow their instructions.

questions.question: To which of the following examinees may a VE not administer an examination?
answers: Relatives of the VE as listed in the FCC rules
questions.explanation: §97.509(d): a VE may not administer an exam to a spouse, child, grandchild, stepchild, parent, grandparent, stepparent, brother, sister, stepbrother, stepsister, aunt, uncle, niece, nephew or in-law.

questions.question: What may be the penalty for a VE who fraudulently administers or certifies an examination?
answers: Revocation of the VE’s amateur station license grant and the suspension of the VE’s amateur operator license grant
A fine of up to $1,000 per occurrence
A sentence of up to one year in prison
questions.explanation: §97.509(e): a VE who fraudulently administers or certifies an exam can have their amateur station license revoked and their operator license suspended.

questions.question: What must the administering VEs do after the administration of a successful examination for an amateur operator license?
answers: They must collect and send the documents directly to the FCC
They must collect and submit the documents to the coordinating VEC for grading
They must submit the application document to the coordinating VEC according to the coordinating VEC instructions
They must return the documents to the applicant for submission to the FCC according to the FCC instructions
questions.explanation: §97.509(m): after a successful exam, the administering VEs submit the application document to the coordinating VEC, following the VEC's instructions.

questions.question: What must the VE team do if an examinee scores a passing grade on all examination elements needed for an upgrade or new license?
answers: Photocopy all examination documents and forward them to the FCC for processing
Three VEs must certify that the examinee is qualified for the license grant and that they have complied with the administering VE requirements
Issue the examinee the new or upgrade license
questions.explanation: §97.509(i): when an examinee passes, three VEs must certify that the examinee is qualified for the license grant and that the VEs complied with the administering-VE requirements.

questions.question: On what frequencies are spread spectrum transmissions permitted?
answers: Only on amateur frequencies above 50 MHz
Only on amateur frequencies above 222 MHz
Only on amateur frequencies above 420 MHz
Only on amateur frequencies above 144 MHz
questions.explanation: §97.305(c): spread spectrum (SS) emissions are authorized only on amateur bands above 222 MHz.

questions.question: What privileges are authorized in the US to persons holding an amateur service license granted by the government of Canada?
answers: None, they must obtain a US license
Full privileges of the General class license on the 80-, 40-, 20-, 15-, and 10-meter bands
The operating terms and conditions of the Canadian amateur service license, not to exceed US Amateur Extra class license privileges
Full privileges, up to and including those of the Amateur Extra class license, on the 80-, 40-, 20-, 15-, and 10-meter bands
questions.explanation: §97.107(a): a Canadian licensee operating in the US may use the operating terms of their Canadian license, but not beyond US Amateur Extra privileges.

questions.question: Under what circumstances may a dealer sell an external RF power amplifier capable of operation below 144 MHz if it has not been granted FCC certification?
answers: Gain is less than 23 dB when driven by power of 10 watts or less
The equipment dealer assembled it from a kit
It was manufactured and certificated in a country which has a reciprocal certification agreement with the FCC
The amplifier is constructed or modified by an amateur radio operator for use at an amateur station
questions.explanation: §97.315(b): an uncertificated external amplifier for use below 144 MHz may be sold to an amateur in a few cases. One is when it was constructed or modified by an amateur radio operator for use at an amateur station.

questions.question: Which of the following geographic descriptions approximately describes "Line A"?
answers: A line roughly parallel to and south of the border between the US and Canada
A line roughly parallel to and west of the US Atlantic coastline
A line roughly parallel to and north of the border between the US and Mexico
A line roughly parallel to and east of the US Pacific coastline
questions.explanation: §97.3(a)(30): Line A runs roughly parallel to and south of the US–Canada border. North of it, some 420–430 MHz operation is prohibited to protect Canadian services.

questions.question: Amateur stations may not transmit in which of the following frequency segments if they are located in the contiguous 48 states and north of Line A?
questions.explanation: §97.303(m)(1): stations in the contiguous US north of Line A may not transmit on 420–430 MHz.

questions.question: Under what circumstances might the FCC issue a Special Temporary Authority (STA) to an amateur station?
answers: To provide for experimental amateur communications
To allow use of a special event call sign
To allow a VE group with less than three VEs to administer examinations in a remote, sparsely populated area
To allow a licensee who has passed an upgrade exam to operate with upgraded privileges while waiting for posting on the FCC database
questions.explanation: §1.931: the FCC may grant an STA for temporary, special-circumstance operation, such as experimental amateur communications not covered by the rules.

questions.question: When may an amateur station send a message to a business?
answers: When the pecuniary interest of the amateur or his or her employer is less than $25
When the pecuniary interest of the amateur or his or her employer is less than $50
When neither the amateur nor their employer has a pecuniary interest in the communications
questions.explanation: §97.113(a)(3): amateurs may communicate with businesses only when neither the amateur nor their employer has a pecuniary interest in the communication.

questions.question: Which of the following types of amateur station communications are prohibited?
answers: Communications transmitted for hire or material compensation, except as otherwise provided in the rules
Communications that have political content, except as allowed by the Fairness Doctrine
Communications in a language other than English
questions.explanation: §97.113(a)(2) prohibits communications for hire or for material compensation, direct or indirect, except where the rules provide otherwise (for example, certain teachers and club station operators).

questions.question: Which of the following cannot be transmitted over an amateur radio mesh network?
answers: Messages encoded to obscure their meaning
questions.explanation: §97.113(a)(4) prohibits messages encoded to obscure their meaning on all amateur stations, including mesh networks. Third-party traffic and email are allowed within the rules.

questions.question: Who may be the control operator of an auxiliary station?
answers: Only Technician, General, Advanced, or Amateur Extra class operators
Only General, Advanced, or Amateur Extra class operators
questions.explanation: §97.201(a): only a holder of a Technician, General, Advanced or Amateur Extra license may be the control operator of an auxiliary station.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes one of the standards that must be met by an external RF power amplifier if it is to qualify for a grant of FCC certification?
answers: It must produce full legal output when driven by not more than 5 watts of mean RF input power
It must have received an Underwriters Laboratory certification for electrical safety as well as having met IEEE standard 14.101(B)
It must exhibit a gain of less than 23 dB when driven by 10 watts or less
It must satisfy the FCC’s spurious emission standards when operated at the lesser of 1500 watts or its full output power
questions.explanation: §97.317: to be certificated, an external amplifier must meet the spurious emission standards when operated at the lesser of 1.5 kW PEP or its full output power.

questions.question: What is the direction of an ascending pass for an amateur satellite?
questions.explanation: An ascending pass is the part of an orbit where the satellite is moving northward, so it comes up from the south and travels south to north. A descending pass goes north to south.

questions.question: Which of the following is characteristic of an inverting linear transponder?
answers: Doppler shift is reduced because the uplink and downlink shifts are in opposite directions
Signal position in the band is reversed
Upper sideband on the uplink becomes lower sideband on the downlink, and vice versa
questions.explanation: An inverting transponder mixes the uplink with a local oscillator and transmits the difference product. That reverses the passband (the high end of the uplink comes out at the low end of the downlink) and swaps USB and LSB. The uplink and downlink Doppler shifts then partly cancel, so all three statements are true.

questions.question: How is an upload signal processed by an inverting linear transponder?
answers: The signal is detected and remodulated on the reverse sideband
The signal is passed through a nonlinear filter
The signal is reduced to I and Q components, and the Q component is filtered out
The signal is mixed with a local oscillator signal and the difference product is transmitted
questions.explanation: The transponder mixes the received band with a local oscillator and retransmits the difference frequency (LO − f), which inverts the spectrum. It does not demodulate the signal.

questions.question: What is meant by the “mode” of an amateur radio satellite?
answers: Whether the satellite is in a low earth or geostationary orbit
The satellite’s uplink and downlink frequency bands
The satellite’s orientation with respect to the Earth
Whether the satellite is in a polar or equatorial orbit
questions.explanation: A satellite's mode describes its uplink and downlink bands. For example, mode U/V means a 70 cm uplink and a 2 m downlink.

questions.question: What do the letters in a satellite’s mode designator specify?
answers: Power limits for uplink and downlink transmissions
The location of the ground control station
The polarization of uplink and downlink signals
The uplink and downlink frequency ranges
questions.explanation: Mode letters name the uplink and downlink frequency bands (for example V = 2 m, U = 70 cm, L = 23 cm, S = 13 cm).

questions.question: What are Keplerian elements?
answers: Parameters that define the orbit of a satellite
Phase reversing elements in a Yagi antenna
High-emission heater filaments used in magnetron tubes
Encrypting codes used for spread spectrum modulation
questions.explanation: Keplerian elements are the set of orbital parameters (inclination, RAAN, eccentricity, argument of perigee, mean anomaly, mean motion, epoch) that tracking programs use to predict where a satellite will be.

questions.question: Which of the following types of signals can be relayed through a linear transponder?
questions.explanation: A linear transponder retransmits everything in its passband faithfully, so any mode can go through it: FM, CW, SSB, SSTV, PSK and packet. FM is discouraged because its constant power uses up the shared downlink power.

questions.question: Why should effective radiated power (ERP) be limited to a satellite that uses a linear transponder?
answers: To prevent creating errors in the satellite telemetry
To avoid reducing the downlink power to all other users
To prevent the satellite from emitting out-of-band signals
To avoid interfering with terrestrial QSOs
questions.explanation: All users share the transponder's limited downlink power. An overly strong uplink takes a bigger share and reduces the downlink power everyone else gets.

questions.question: What do the terms “L band” and “S band” specify?
questions.explanation: In amateur satellite usage, L band is 23 cm (1.2 GHz) and S band is 13 cm (2.4 GHz).

questions.question: What type of satellite appears to stay in one position in the sky?
questions.explanation: A geostationary satellite orbits above the equator at about 35,786 km with a 24-hour period, so it appears fixed in the sky. QO-100 is an amateur example.

questions.question: What type of antenna can be used to minimize the effects of spin modulation and Faraday rotation?
questions.explanation: Circular polarization receives signals of any linear polarization angle, so the polarization changes from satellite spin and Faraday rotation cause much less fading.

questions.question: What is the purpose of digital store-and-forward functions on an amateur radio satellite?
answers: To upload operational software for the transponder
To delay download of telemetry between satellites
To hold digital messages in the satellite for later download
questions.explanation: Store-and-forward satellites ("PACSATs") receive digital messages, keep them in memory, and download them later when the satellite passes over the destination ground station.

questions.question: In digital television, what does a coding rate of 3/4 mean?
answers: 25% of the data sent is forward error correction data
Data compression reduces data rate by 3/4
1/4 of the time interval is used as a guard interval
Three, four-bit words are used to transmit each pixel
questions.explanation: A code rate of 3/4 means 3 of every 4 bits are payload and 1 of every 4 (25%) is forward error correction redundancy.

questions.question: How many horizontal lines make up a fast-scan (NTSC) television frame?
questions.explanation: An NTSC frame has 525 horizontal lines, sent as two interlaced fields of 262.5 lines each, at about 30 frames per second.

questions.question: How is an interlaced scanning pattern generated in a fast-scan (NTSC) television system?
answers: By scanning each field from bottom-to-top
By scanning lines from left-to-right in one field and right-to-left in the next
By scanning odd-numbered lines in one field and even-numbered lines in the next
questions.explanation: Interlacing sends the odd-numbered lines in one field and the even-numbered lines in the next field, giving 60 fields per second and less flicker.

questions.question: How is color information sent in analog SSTV?
answers: Color information is sent on a 2.8 kHz subcarrier
Color is sent in a color burst at the end of each line
Color is amplitude modulated on the frequency modulated intensity signal
questions.explanation: Analog color SSTV modes such as Martin and Scottie send the color components (for example green, blue, red) as separate scan lines, one after another.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the use of vestigial sideband in analog fast-scan TV transmissions?
answers: The vestigial sideband carries the audio information
The vestigial sideband contains chroma information
Vestigial sideband reduces the bandwidth while increasing the fidelity of low frequency video components
Vestigial sideband provides high frequency emphasis to sharpen the picture
questions.explanation: VSB transmits one full sideband and only part of the other. That saves bandwidth compared with full AM, while keeping the low-frequency video components that a pure SSB filter would distort.

questions.question: What is vestigial sideband modulation?
answers: Amplitude modulation in which one complete sideband and a portion of the other are transmitted
A type of modulation in which one sideband is inverted
Narrow-band FM modulation achieved by filtering one sideband from the audio before frequency modulating the carrier
Spread spectrum modulation achieved by applying FM modulation following single sideband amplitude modulation
questions.explanation: Vestigial sideband is AM in which one complete sideband and a portion (vestige) of the other sideband are transmitted.

questions.question: Which types of modulation are used for amateur television DVB-T signals?
questions.explanation: DVB-T uses OFDM, with each subcarrier modulated by QPSK or QAM (16- or 64-QAM).

questions.question: What technique allows commercial analog TV receivers to be used for fast-scan TV operations on the 70-centimeter band?
answers: Transmitting on channels shared with cable TV
Transmitting on the abandoned TV channel 2
Using USB and demodulating the signal with a computer sound card
questions.explanation: Some 70 cm ATV frequencies fall on cable TV channels (for example channels 57–61). A cable-ready analog TV can tune them directly.
questions.explanationNote: Exact cable channel numbers paraphrased.

questions.question: What kind of receiver can be used to receive and decode SSTV using the Digital Radio Mondiale (DRM) protocol?
questions.explanation: DRM digital SSTV fits in a voice channel, so it is sent and received on an ordinary SSB transceiver with the decoding done by computer software.

questions.question: What aspect of an analog slow-scan television signal encodes the brightness of the picture?
questions.explanation: Analog SSTV is frequency modulated: brightness is set by the tone frequency, from 1500 Hz (black) to 2300 Hz (white). Sync pulses are at 1200 Hz.

questions.question: What is the function of the vertical interval signaling (VIS) code sent as part of an SSTV transmission?
answers: To lock the color burst oscillator in color SSTV images
To identify the SSTV mode being used
To identify the call sign of the station transmitting
questions.explanation: The VIS (Vertical Interval Signaling) code at the start of a transmission is a short digital tone sequence that tells the receiving software which SSTV mode is in use.

questions.question: What signals SSTV receiving software to begin a new picture line?
questions.explanation: Each line begins with a sync pulse at a specific tone frequency (1200 Hz), which the decoder detects to start a new line.

questions.question: What indicator is required to be used by US-licensed operators when operating a station via remote control and the remote transmitter is located in the US?
answers: / followed by the USPS two-letter abbreviation for the state in which the remote station is located
/R# where # is the district of the remote station
/ followed by the ARRL Section of the remote station
questions.explanation: For remote operation of a station located in the US, the FCC requires only normal identification with your own call sign. No portable or remote indicator is required.

questions.question: Which of the following file formats is used for exchanging amateur radio log data?
questions.explanation: ADIF (Amateur Data Interchange Format) is the standard file format for exchanging log data between logging programs, LoTW, QRZ and similar services.

questions.question: From which of the following bands is amateur radio contesting generally excluded?
questions.explanation: By convention (IARU band plans) contests are not held on the WARC bands: 30 m, 17 m and 12 m.

questions.question: Which of the following frequencies can be used for amateur radio mesh networks?
answers: HF frequencies where digital communications are permitted
Frequencies shared with various unlicensed wireless data services
The 60-meter band channel centered on 5373 kHz
questions.explanation: Amateur mesh networks (for example AREDN) use 2.4, 3.4 and 5.8 GHz channels that are shared with unlicensed Part 15 Wi-Fi devices.

questions.question: What is the function of a DX QSL Manager?
answers: Handle the receiving and sending of confirmations for a DX station
Run a net to allow many stations to contact a rare DX station
Communicate to a DXpedition about propagation, band openings, pileup conditions, etc.
questions.explanation: A QSL manager handles the incoming and outgoing QSL card and confirmation work for a DX station or DXpedition.

questions.question: During a VHF/UHF contest, in which band segment would you expect to find the highest level of SSB or CW activity?
answers: At the top of each band, usually in a segment reserved for contests
In the middle of each band, usually on the national calling frequency
In the weak signal segment of the band, with most of the activity near the calling frequency
In the middle of the band, usually 25 kHz above the national calling frequency
questions.explanation: VHF/UHF SSB and CW contest activity is concentrated in the weak-signal segment, near the calling frequency (for example 50.125, 144.200 and 432.100 MHz).

questions.question: What is the Cabrillo format?
answers: A standard for submission of electronic contest logs
A method of exchanging information during a contest QSO
The most common set of contest rules
A digital protocol specifically designed for rapid contest exchanges
questions.explanation: Cabrillo is the standard text format for submitting electronic contest logs to sponsors.

questions.question: Which of the following contacts may be confirmed through the Logbook of The World (LoTW)?
answers: Special event contacts between stations in the US
Contacts between a US station and a non-US station
Contacts for Worked All States credit
questions.explanation: LoTW confirms any valid QSO in which both stations upload matching records: US-to-US, special event, or DX contacts. It supports awards such as WAS and DXCC, so all the choices are correct.

questions.question: What type of equipment is commonly used to implement an amateur radio mesh network?
answers: A 2-meter VHF transceiver with a 1,200-baud modem
A computer running EchoLink to provide interface from the radio to the internet
A wireless router running custom firmware
A 440 MHz transceiver with a 9,600-baud modem
questions.explanation: Amateur mesh nodes are usually commercial Wi-Fi routers reflashed with amateur firmware (AREDN), often operating at higher power under Part 97.

questions.question: Why do DX stations often transmit and receive on different frequencies?
answers: Because the DX station may be transmitting on a frequency that is prohibited to some responding stations
To separate the calling stations from the DX station
To improve operating efficiency by reducing interference
questions.explanation: Working split avoids answering on frequencies some callers aren't permitted to use, keeps the pileup off the DX station's transmit frequency, and makes the DX station more efficient. All the reasons apply.

questions.question: How should you generally identify your station when attempting to contact a DX station during a contest or in a pileup?
answers: Send your full call sign once or twice
Send only the last two letters of your call sign until you make contact
Send your full call sign and grid square
Send the call sign of the DX station three times, the words “this is,” then your call sign three times
questions.explanation: Sending your full call once or twice is the courteous, efficient practice. Partial calls and long repeated calls slow down the pileup.

questions.question: What indicates the delay between a control operator action and the corresponding change in the transmitted signal?
questions.explanation: Latency is the delay between a control action, such as keying at the remote operator position, and the resulting change in the transmitted signal.

questions.question: Which of the following digital modes is designed for meteor scatter communications?
questions.explanation: MSK144 is the WSJT-X mode designed for the short, bursty propagation of meteor scatter.

questions.question: What information replaces signal-to-noise ratio when using the FT8 or FT4 modes in a VHF contest?
questions.explanation: VHF contests require a grid square exchange, so in the FT8/FT4 contest modes the grid replaces the SNR report.

questions.question: Which of the following digital modes is designed for EME communications?
questions.explanation: Q65 is designed for weak, Doppler-spread paths such as EME and ionospheric scatter. It can average across transmissions to decode very weak signals.

questions.question: What technology is used for real-time tracking of balloons carrying amateur radio transmitters?
questions.explanation: APRS position packets, often relayed by digipeaters and iGates to the internet, are the usual way to track high-altitude balloons in real time.

questions.question: What is the characteristic of the JT65 mode?
answers: Decodes signals with a very low signal-to-noise ratio
Permits fast-scan TV transmissions over narrow bandwidth
questions.explanation: JT65 uses strong error correction and long, slow transmissions, so it can decode signals well below the noise (around −25 dB SNR in 2.5 kHz).

questions.question: Which of the following is a method for establishing EME contacts?
answers: Judging optimum transmission times by monitoring beacons reflected from the moon
High-speed CW identification to avoid fading
questions.explanation: EME stations transmit and receive in alternating, time-synchronized periods (for example 1-minute periods for JT65 or Q65), so each station knows when to listen.

questions.question: What digital protocol is used by APRS?
questions.explanation: APRS uses the AX.25 packet radio protocol.

questions.question: What type of packet frame is used to transmit APRS beacon data?
questions.explanation: APRS beacons are sent as AX.25 Unnumbered Information (UI) frames. These are connectionless broadcasts that need no acknowledgment.

questions.question: What type of modulation is used by JT65?
questions.explanation: JT65 uses 65-tone frequency-shift keying, i.e. multitone AFSK.

questions.question: What does the packet path WIDE3-1 designate?
answers: Three stations are allowed on frequency, one transmitting at a time
Three subcarriers are permitted, subcarrier one is being used
Three digipeater hops are requested with one remaining
Three internet gateway stations may receive one transmission
questions.explanation: In WIDEn-N, n is the number of hops requested and N is the number remaining. WIDE3-1 means 3 hops were requested and 1 is left.

questions.question: How do APRS stations relay data?
questions.explanation: APRS packets are relayed by digipeaters, which receive and retransmit them on the same frequency.

questions.question: Which of the following types of modulation is used for data emissions below 30 MHz?
answers: DTMF tones modulating an FM signal
questions.explanation: Most HF data emissions (RTTY, PSK modes, PACTOR and others) are forms of frequency- or phase-shift keying. FSK is the classic example.

questions.question: Which of the following synchronizes WSJT-X digital mode transmit/receive timing?
questions.explanation: WSJT-X modes transmit and receive in fixed time slots, so the computer clocks at both ends must be accurate to within about a second, usually by NTP or GPS.

questions.question: To what does the "4" in FT4 refer?
answers: Multiples of 4 bits of user information
questions.explanation: FT4 uses 4-tone continuous-phase FSK (4-GFSK).

questions.question: Which of the following is characteristic of the FST4 mode?
questions.explanation: FST4 uses 4-GFSK, offers variable T/R periods (15 s to 30 min), and several tone spacings. Per the pool key, all the statements are correct.
questions.explanationNote: FST4 'seven tone spacings' detail not independently verified; explanation follows pool key.

questions.question: Which of these digital modes does not support keyboard-to-keyboard operation?
questions.explanation: WSPR only sends beacon reports (call, grid, power) for propagation study. It cannot carry free keyboard-to-keyboard text.

questions.question: What is the length of an FT8 transmission cycle?
answers: It varies with the amount of data
questions.explanation: FT8 uses 15-second transmit/receive periods.

questions.question: How does Q65 differ from JT65?
questions.explanation: Q65 can average multiple receive cycles to decode signals too weak to copy in any single period, which is very useful for EME. JT65 decodes each period separately.

questions.question: Which of the following HF digital modes can be used to transfer binary files?
questions.explanation: PACTOR is an ARQ mode with error-free binary transfer, so it can send binary files. The others are character-based.

questions.question: Which of the following HF digital modes uses variable-length character coding?
questions.explanation: PSK31 uses Varicode, a variable-length code in which frequent characters get shorter codes.

questions.question: Which of these digital modes has the narrowest bandwidth?
questions.explanation: An FT8 signal is about 50 Hz wide. MFSK16 is about 316 Hz, 170 Hz RTTY is about 250 Hz, and PACTOR IV is about 2.4 kHz.

questions.question: What is the difference between direct FSK and audio FSK?
answers: Direct FSK modulates the transmitter VFO
Direct FSK can transmit higher baud rates
questions.explanation: Direct FSK shifts the transmitter's VFO or oscillator directly. AFSK feeds audio tones into an SSB transmitter.

questions.question: How do ALE stations establish contact?
answers: ALE constantly scans a list of frequencies, activating the radio when the designated call sign is received
ALE radios monitor an internet site for the frequency they are being paged on
ALE radios send a constant tone code to establish a frequency for future use
ALE radios activate when they hear their signal echoed by back scatter
questions.explanation: ALE radios keep scanning a programmed list of frequencies. When one hears a call addressed to its call sign it stops and alerts the operator, and the link is set up on that frequency.

questions.question: Which of these digital modes has the highest data throughput under clear communication conditions?
questions.explanation: PACTOR IV uses adaptive high-order modulation in about 2.4 kHz and reaches several kbit/s on good paths, far faster than the other modes listed.

questions.question: What is the approximate maximum separation measured along the surface of the Earth between two stations communicating by EME?
answers: 2,000 miles, if the moon is at perigee
2,000 miles, if the moon is at apogee
5,000 miles, if the moon is at perigee
12,000 miles, if the moon is “visible” by both stations
questions.explanation: The only requirement for EME is that both stations can see the Moon at the same time. Stations nearly on opposite sides of the Earth can do that, so the separation can reach about 12,000 miles.

questions.question: What characterizes libration fading of an EME signal?
answers: A slow change in the pitch of the CW signal
A gradual loss of signal as the sun rises
The returning echo is several hertz lower in frequency than the transmitted signal
questions.explanation: The Moon's libration (its apparent rocking) makes reflections from different parts of its rough surface add and cancel as they change. The result is a rapid, fluttery, irregular fade.

questions.question: When scheduling EME contacts, which of these conditions will generally result in the least path loss?
answers: When the Moon is at perigee
When the Moon is at apogee
When the MUF is above 30 MHz
questions.explanation: Path loss rises with distance. At perigee the Moon is about 10% closer than at apogee, which saves roughly 2 dB of round-trip path loss.

questions.question: In what direction does an electromagnetic wave travel?
answers: It depends on the phase angle of the magnetic field
It travels parallel to the electric and magnetic fields
It depends on the phase angle of the electric field
It travels at a right angle to the electric and magnetic fields
questions.explanation: An EM wave travels at right angles to both its electric and magnetic fields, in the direction of the Poynting vector E × H.

questions.question: How are the component fields of an electromagnetic wave oriented?
answers: They are 90 degrees out of phase
questions.explanation: In a radiated EM wave, the E and H fields are perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel. In the far field they are also in phase.

questions.question: What should be done to continue a long-distance contact when the MUF for that path decreases due to darkness?
answers: Switch to a higher frequency HF band
Switch to a lower frequency HF band
Change to an antenna with a higher takeoff angle
Change to an antenna with greater beam width
questions.explanation: Ionization drops after dark and the MUF falls with it. Moving to a lower band keeps the frequency below the MUF so the path stays open.

questions.question: Atmospheric ducts capable of propagating microwave signals often form over what geographic feature?
questions.explanation: Temperature and humidity inversions form readily over large bodies of water. The resulting ducts can guide VHF and microwave signals far beyond line of sight.

questions.question: When a meteor strikes the Earth’s atmosphere, a linear ionized region is formed at what region of the ionosphere?
questions.explanation: Meteors burn up at roughly 85–120 km altitude, the E region, and leave ionized trails that can reflect radio signals.

questions.question: Which of the following frequency ranges is most suited for meteor-scatter communications?
questions.explanation: Meteor trails reflect best from about 28 MHz to 148 MHz (10 m, 6 m and 2 m). 6 m is the classic band for it.

questions.question: What determines the speed of electromagnetic waves through a medium?
questions.explanation: Wave velocity in a medium is v = c/n, where n is the index of refraction.

questions.question: What is a typical range for tropospheric duct propagation of microwave signals?
questions.explanation: Microwave tropospheric ducts commonly support paths of about 100–300 miles. Much longer paths sometimes occur.

questions.question: What is most likely to result in auroral propagation?
answers: Extreme low-pressure areas in polar regions
questions.explanation: Severe geomagnetic storms push the aurora toward lower latitudes. The ionized auroral curtain scatters VHF and HF signals.

questions.question: Which of these emission modes is best for auroral propagation?
questions.explanation: Auroral reflection adds heavy Doppler spreading, so voice comes through as a raspy buzz. CW is the narrowest, most copyable mode under those conditions.

questions.question: What are circularly polarized electromagnetic waves?
answers: Waves with an electric field bent into a circular shape
Waves with rotating electric and magnetic fields
Waves produced by a loop antenna
questions.explanation: In a circularly polarized wave, the E and H fields rotate around the direction of travel, completing one full turn every wavelength.

questions.question: Where is transequatorial propagation (TEP) most likely to occur?
answers: Between points separated by 2,000 miles to 3,000 miles over a path perpendicular to the geomagnetic equator
Between points located 1,500 miles to 2,000 miles apart on the geomagnetic equator
Between points located at each other’s antipode
Through the region where the terminator crosses the geographic equator
questions.explanation: TEP crosses the geomagnetic equator on north–south paths of roughly 2,000–3,000 miles, between stations at similar distances north and south of it.

questions.question: What is the approximate maximum range for signals using transequatorial propagation?
questions.explanation: TEP can support paths up to about 5,000 miles.

questions.question: At what time of day is transequatorial propagation most likely to occur?
questions.explanation: TEP is strongest in the afternoon and early evening, when the equatorial ionization bulges are fully developed.

questions.question: What are “extraordinary” and “ordinary” waves?
answers: Extraordinary waves exhibit rare long-skip propagation, compared to ordinary waves, which travel shorter distances
Independently propagating, elliptically polarized waves created in the ionosphere
questions.explanation: The geomagnetic field splits a wave entering the ionosphere into two elliptically polarized components, the ordinary and extraordinary waves. They propagate independently and refract differently.

questions.question: Which of the following paths is most likely to support long-distance propagation on 160 meters?
questions.explanation: 160 m signals are heavily absorbed by the daytime D layer, so long-distance contacts need a path that is entirely in darkness.

questions.question: On which of the following amateur bands is long-path propagation most frequent?
questions.explanation: Long-path propagation, the long way around the great circle, is most common on 40 m and 20 m.

questions.question: What effect does lowering a signal’s transmitted elevation angle have on ionospheric HF skip propagation?
answers: The distance covered by each hop increases
questions.explanation: A lower takeoff angle hits the ionosphere farther away, so each hop covers more ground.

questions.question: How does the maximum range of ground-wave propagation change when the signal frequency is increased?
questions.explanation: Ground-wave losses increase with frequency, so its range is greatest on LF and MF and shrinks as the frequency rises.

questions.question: At what time of year is sporadic-E propagation most likely to occur?
answers: Around the solstices, especially the summer solstice
Around the solstices, especially the winter solstice
Around the equinoxes, especially the spring equinox
Around the equinoxes, especially the fall equinox
questions.explanation: Sporadic-E peaks around the solstices, most of all near the summer solstice (May–August in the Northern Hemisphere), with a smaller peak in winter.

questions.question: What is the effect of chordal-hop propagation?
answers: The signal experiences less loss compared to multi-hop propagation, which uses Earth as a reflector
The MUF for chordal-hop propagation is much lower than for normal skip propagation
Atmospheric noise is reduced in the direction of chordal-hop propagation
Signals travel faster along ionospheric chords
questions.explanation: In chordal hop the signal refracts several times along the ionosphere without bouncing off the ground in between, so it avoids the ground-reflection losses of normal multi-hop.

questions.question: At what time of day is sporadic-E propagation most likely to occur?
questions.explanation: Sporadic-E is mainly a daytime phenomenon, most likely between sunrise and sunset. It often peaks in mid-morning and early evening.

questions.question: What is chordal-hop propagation?
answers: Propagation away from the great circle bearing between stations
Successive ionospheric refractions without an intermediate reflection from the ground
Signals reflected back toward the transmitting station
questions.explanation: Chordal hop is a series of ionospheric refractions with no intermediate reflection from the ground.

questions.question: What type of polarization is supported by ground-wave propagation?
questions.explanation: Ground wave needs vertical polarization. The Earth effectively shorts out a horizontally polarized ground wave.

questions.question: What is the cause of short-term radio blackouts?
questions.explanation: The X-ray and UV burst from a solar flare reaches Earth in about 8 minutes. It ionizes the D layer heavily and causes sudden HF blackouts on the daylit side.

questions.question: What is indicated by a rising A-index or K-index?
answers: Increasing disturbance of the geomagnetic field
Decreasing disturbance of the geomagnetic field
Higher levels of solar UV radiation
An increase in the critical frequency
questions.explanation: The K-index (3-hour) and A-index (daily) measure geomagnetic activity. Rising values mean a more disturbed field.

questions.question: Which of the following signal paths is most likely to experience high levels of absorption when the A-index or K-index is elevated?
questions.explanation: When geomagnetic activity is high, paths that pass through the auroral oval at high latitudes suffer strong absorption.

questions.question: What does the value of Bz (B sub z) represent?
answers: North-south strength of the interplanetary magnetic field
questions.explanation: Bz is the north–south component of the interplanetary magnetic field carried by the solar wind.

questions.question: What orientation of Bz (B sub z) increases the likelihood that charged particles from the Sun will cause disturbed conditions?
questions.explanation: A southward Bz couples with Earth's northward-pointing field and lets solar wind energy and particles in, which drives geomagnetic storms.

questions.question: How does the VHF/UHF radio horizon compare to the geographic horizon?
questions.explanation: Atmospheric refraction bends VHF and UHF waves slightly back toward Earth, so the radio horizon is about 15% farther than the optical one: d ≈ 1.415√h(ft) miles, versus about 1.23√h for the optical horizon.

questions.question: Which of the following indicates the greatest solar flare intensity?
questions.explanation: Solar flare classes, from weakest to strongest, are A, B, C, M and X. Each class is 10 times stronger than the one before, so X is the strongest.

questions.question: Which of the following is the space-weather term for an extreme geomagnetic storm?
questions.explanation: On NOAA's geomagnetic storm scale, G5 is the extreme level. X5 and M9 are flare classes.

questions.question: What type of data is reported by amateur radio propagation reporting networks?
questions.explanation: Networks such as the Reverse Beacon Network, PSK Reporter and WSPRnet report actual received CW and digital-mode signals, giving real-time propagation data.

questions.question: What does the 304A solar parameter measure?
answers: The ratio of X-ray flux to radio flux, correlated to sunspot number
UV emissions at 304 angstroms, correlated to the solar flux index
The solar wind velocity at an angle of 304 degrees from the solar equator, correlated to geomagnetic storms
The solar emission at 304 GHz, correlated to X-ray flare levels
questions.explanation: 304 Å is the extreme-ultraviolet He II emission line. It tracks solar activity and correlates with the solar flux index.

questions.question: What does VOACAP software model?
questions.explanation: VOACAP (Voice of America Coverage Analysis Program) predicts HF skywave propagation and reliability.

questions.question: Which of the following is indicated by a sudden rise in radio background noise across a large portion of the HF spectrum?
answers: A coronal mass ejection impact or a solar flare has occurred
Transequatorial propagation on 6 meters is likely
Long-path propagation on the higher HF bands is likely
questions.explanation: A sudden rise in broadband HF noise accompanies solar radio bursts from flares and CME-driven disturbances.
questions.explanationNote: Mechanism (solar radio burst noise) stated generally.

questions.question: Which of the following limits the highest frequency signal that can be accurately displayed on a digital oscilloscope?
answers: Sampling rate of the analog-to-digital converter
questions.explanation: By the Nyquist criterion, a sampled signal can be reproduced accurately only up to half the ADC sample rate. So the sampling rate sets the highest frequency a digital scope can show correctly.

questions.question: Which of the following parameters does a spectrum analyzer display on the vertical and horizontal axes?
questions.explanation: A spectrum analyzer is a frequency-domain instrument: amplitude on the vertical axis, frequency on the horizontal.

questions.question: Which of the following test instruments is used to display spurious signals and/or intermodulation distortion products generated by an SSB transmitter?
questions.explanation: Spurs and IMD products are separate signals at other frequencies. A spectrum analyzer shows them, and their levels relative to the carrier.

questions.question: How is compensation of an oscilloscope probe performed?
answers: A square wave is displayed, and the probe is adjusted until the horizontal portions of the displayed wave are as nearly flat as possible
A high frequency sine wave is displayed, and the probe is adjusted for maximum amplitude
A frequency standard is displayed, and the probe is adjusted until the deflection time is accurate
A DC voltage standard is displayed, and the probe is adjusted until the displayed voltage is accurate
questions.explanation: Probe compensation adjusts the probe's capacitive divider to match the scope input. With the scope's square-wave calibrator displayed, you trim the probe until the tops and bottoms are flat, with no overshoot and no rounding.

questions.question: What is the purpose of using a prescaler with a frequency counter?
answers: Amplify low-level signals for more accurate counting
Multiply a higher frequency signal so a low-frequency counter can display the operating frequency
Prevent oscillation in a low-frequency counter circuit
Reduce the signal frequency to within the counter's operating range
questions.explanation: A prescaler divides the input frequency by a known factor (for example ÷10) so it falls within the counter's range. The reading is then scaled back up.

questions.question: What is the effect of aliasing on a digital oscilloscope when displaying a waveform?
answers: A false, jittery low-frequency version of the waveform is displayed
The waveform DC offset will be inaccurate
Calibration of the vertical scale is no longer valid
Excessive blanking occurs, which prevents display of the waveform
questions.explanation: When a signal is sampled below its Nyquist rate, it aliases: the scope shows a false lower-frequency waveform that often looks unstable or jittery.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of using an antenna analyzer compared to an SWR bridge?
answers: Antenna analyzers automatically tune your antenna for resonance
Antenna analyzers compute SWR and impedance automatically
Antenna analyzers display a time-varying representation of the modulation envelope
questions.explanation: An antenna analyzer has its own low-power signal source and computes SWR, impedance (R ± jX) and related values at any frequency. A simple SWR bridge only indicates SWR while you transmit.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to measure SWR?
questions.explanation: A directional wattmeter (forward/reflected), a VNA and an antenna analyzer can all determine SWR.

questions.question: Which of the following is good practice when using an oscilloscope probe?
answers: Minimize the length of the probe's ground connection
Never use a high-impedance probe to measure a low-impedance circuit
Never use a DC-coupled probe to measure an AC circuit
questions.explanation: A long probe ground lead adds inductance, which causes ringing and pickup. Keep the ground connection as short as possible.

questions.question: Which trigger mode is most effective when using an oscilloscope to measure a linear power supply’s output ripple?
questions.explanation: Line triggering syncs the sweep to the AC mains, so ripple at 60 or 120 Hz stands still on the screen.

questions.question: Which of the following can be measured with an antenna analyzer?
answers: Resonant frequency of a tuned circuit
questions.explanation: An antenna analyzer can find resonance, and with time-domain or open/short methods it can measure a cable's electrical length and velocity factor. All the choices are correct.

questions.question: Which of the following factors most affects the accuracy of a frequency counter?
questions.explanation: A frequency counter counts cycles during a gate time set by its time base. Any error in the time base shows up directly in the reading.

questions.question: What is the significance of voltmeter sensitivity expressed in ohms per volt?
answers: The full scale reading of the voltmeter multiplied by its ohms per volt rating is the input impedance of the voltmeter
The reading in volts multiplied by the ohms per volt rating will determine the power drawn by the device under test
The reading in ohms divided by the ohms per volt rating will determine the voltage applied to the circuit
The full scale reading in amps divided by ohms per volt rating will determine the size of shunt needed
questions.explanation: Input resistance = full-scale voltage × ohms-per-volt. For example, a 20,000 Ω/V meter on its 10 V range presents 200 kΩ.

questions.question: Which S parameter is equivalent to forward gain?
questions.explanation: S21 is the signal coming out of port 2 when port 1 is driven, i.e. forward transmission or gain.

questions.question: Which S parameter represents input port return loss or reflection coefficient (equivalent to VSWR)?
questions.explanation: S11 is the reflection at port 1, the input reflection coefficient. It relates directly to return loss and VSWR.

questions.question: What three test loads are used to calibrate an RF vector network analyzer?
answers: Short circuit, open circuit, and 50 ohms
Short circuit, open circuit, and resonant circuit
50 ohms through 1/8 wavelength, 1/4 wavelength, and 1/2 wavelength of coaxial cable
questions.explanation: SOL calibration uses short, open and load (50 Ω) standards. They let the VNA remove its own systematic errors.

questions.question: How much power is being absorbed by the load when a directional power meter connected between a transmitter and a terminating load reads 100 watts forward power and 25 watts reflected power?
questions.explanation: Power absorbed by the load = forward − reflected = 100 − 25 = 75 W.

questions.question: What do the subscripts of S parameters represent?
answers: The port or ports at which measurements are made
questions.explanation: In Sxy, x is the port where the signal is measured and y is the port being driven.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to determine the Q of a series-tuned circuit?
answers: The ratio of inductive reactance to capacitive reactance
The bandwidth of the circuit's frequency response
The resonant frequency of the circuit
questions.explanation: Q = f0 / BW(−3 dB). Measuring the response bandwidth around resonance therefore gives Q.

questions.question: Which of the following can be measured by a two-port vector network analyzer?
questions.explanation: A two-port VNA measures S21 versus frequency, which is the filter's frequency response (insertion loss and passband shape).

questions.question: Which of the following methods measures intermodulation distortion in an SSB transmitter?
answers: Modulate the transmitter using two RF signals having non-harmonically related frequencies and observe the RF output with a spectrum analyzer
Modulate the transmitter using two AF signals having non-harmonically related frequencies and observe the RF output with a spectrum analyzer
Modulate the transmitter using two AF signals having harmonically related frequencies and observe the RF output with a peak reading wattmeter
Modulate the transmitter using two RF signals having harmonically related frequencies and observe the RF output with a logic analyzer
questions.explanation: The two-tone test feeds two non-harmonically related audio tones into the transmitter and looks at the RF output on a spectrum analyzer for IMD products at 2f1−f2 and 2f2−f1.

questions.question: Which of the following can be measured with a vector network analyzer?
questions.explanation: A VNA measures complex reflection and transmission, so it gives input and output impedance and reflection coefficient. All the choices are correct.

questions.question: What is an effect of excessive phase noise in an SDR receiver’s master clock oscillator?
answers: It limits the receiver’s ability to receive strong signals
It can affect the receiver’s frequency calibration
It decreases the receiver’s third-order intercept point
It can combine with strong signals on nearby frequencies to generate interference
questions.explanation: In reciprocal mixing, phase noise on the SDR clock or LO mixes with strong nearby signals and puts noise and interference on top of weak desired signals.

questions.question: Which of the following receiver circuits can be effective in eliminating interference from strong out-of-band signals?
questions.explanation: A front-end filter or preselector removes strong out-of-band signals before they reach the first amplifier and mixer, where they could cause overload or IMD.

questions.question: What is the term for the suppression in an FM receiver of one signal by another stronger signal on the same frequency?
questions.explanation: In FM, the capture effect lets the stronger of two co-channel signals take over the demodulator and suppress the weaker one.

questions.question: What is the noise figure of a receiver?
answers: The ratio of atmospheric noise to phase noise
The ratio of the noise bandwidth in hertz to the theoretical bandwidth of a resistive network
The ratio in dB of the noise generated in the receiver to atmospheric noise
The ratio in dB of the noise generated by the receiver to the theoretical minimum noise
questions.explanation: Noise figure (dB) compares the noise the receiver actually adds with that of an ideal noiseless receiver (thermal noise only): NF = 10 log(F).

questions.question: What does a receiver noise floor of -174 dBm represent?
answers: The receiver noise is 6 dB above the theoretical minimum
The theoretical noise in a 1 Hz bandwidth at the input of a perfect receiver at room temperature
The noise figure of a 1 Hz bandwidth receiver
The receiver noise is 3 dB above theoretical minimum
questions.explanation: kTB at 290 K in 1 Hz is −174 dBm. That is the thermal noise floor of a perfect receiver per hertz of bandwidth.
